All test components are rated for 10.0 bar gauge. The bench instruction requires filling with water while the high-point vent is open until bubble-free water exits, then closing the vent before pressurization. Raise the pressure to 6.00 bar gauge, isolate the hand pump, and start the hold timer only after isolation. Do not add water during the 300 s hold. A test passes only if the pressure drop is no more than 0.20 bar and there is no visible water leakage during the hold. After assessing the result, use the release valve to depressurize and confirm 0 bar gauge before disconnecting. The completed test log shows 6.00 bar at the start of the isolated hold, 5.90 bar after 300 s, and no visible leakage throughout. Include the acceptance criteria and the verdict for this log.

golden.request: Describe a logic circuit where an indicator light would be lit when either the forward or aft cabin door is open and the braking system is engaged. Include: logic, polarity, and gates in the response.
golden.source: The owner's question, sent verbatim. The key is the owner's answer (2026-10-01): positive logic; doors into an OR gate; the OR output and brake-engaged into an AND gate; the AND output lights the indicator.

items.item: forward and aft doors into an OR gate
OR output and brake-engaged into an AND gate
the AND output lights the indicator

golden.model_answer: This logic circuit would use positive logic polarity where a 1, true, or high means voltage is present and the condition is active. The forward and aft cabin doors would be inputs to an OR gate because a true output is made if either door is open or both are open. The OR gate output would then be an input into an AND gate. The braking system engaged/disengaged would be the other input to the AND gate. The AND gate would only send an output to illuminate the indicator light if either or both doors are open and the braking system is engaged.

wrong.text: Use positive logic: 1 means active. The forward and aft door signals feed an XOR gate, whose output and the brake-engaged signal feed an AND gate that illuminates the indicator light.
Use positive logic: 1 means active. The forward door, aft door and brake-engaged signals all feed one three-input AND gate, which illuminates the indicator light.

variants_must_pass: Assume active-high logic (HIGH = condition true). A 2-input OR gate combines FWD_DOOR_OPEN and AFT_DOOR_OPEN; its output and BRAKE_ENGAGED drive a 2-input AND gate whose output turns on the indicator lamp: LAMP = (FWD + AFT)·BRAKE.

side_test.request: what are the qualifaications for inspection auth regaurding major alterations, (FAA-AMT),https://www.ecfr.gov/ is a good source
side_test.source: The owner's question, sent verbatim, typos included. Key checked by the advisor 2026-10-01 against 14 CFR 65.91, 65.92, 65.93 (govinfo 2024 XML) and 65.95 (LII).

core_items.item: A&P, both ratings, in effect at least 3 years (65.91(c)(1))
actively engaged for the 2-year period before applying (65.91(c)(2))
return to service after a major alteration only with technical data approved by the Administrator (65.95(a)(1))
all: approved (?:technical )?data|technical data approved|data approved by the administrator|faa[- ]approved (?:technical )?data

supplementary_items.item: expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year (65.92)
renewal activity per year: 1 annual or 2 major repairs/alterations per 90 days, progressive, 8-hour refresher, or oral test (65.93)
retest no sooner than 90 days after failing (65.91(d))

side_test.model_answer: Under 14 CFR 65.91, to be eligible for an inspection authorization you must hold a currently effective mechanic certificate with both airframe and powerplant ratings, each in effect for at least 3 years; have been actively engaged for at least the 2-year period before applying in maintaining certificated aircraft; have a fixed base of operations; have the equipment, facilities and inspection data needed; and pass a written test on inspecting for return to service after major repairs and major alterations. An applicant who fails may not retest until 90 days after failing. Under 14 CFR 65.95(a)(1), an IA may inspect and approve for return to service an aircraft after a major repair or major alteration only if the work was done in accordance with technical data approved by the Administrator (not aircraft on a part 121 continuous airworthiness program). The IA expires March 31 of each odd-numbered year (65.92). Renewal (65.93) needs, in each year, one activity such as one annual inspection per 90 days, two major repairs or major alterations per 90 days, a progressive inspection, an 8-hour refresher course, or an oral test.
